Blue is a primary color located between violet and cyan, associated with calmness, trust, and intelligence. Common shades include navy, azure, sky, and cyan, often produced by pigments like Prussian blue. It is a dominant color in nature (sky/sea) due to Rayleigh scattering and is heavily used in fashion for professional, calming, or vibrant looks. Psychological Effects of Blue Calmness & Serenity: Blue evokes tranquility and is often associated with the vastness of the sky and sea. Trust & Dependability: It is frequently used in branding to convey stability, intelligence, and trustworthiness, which is why many social media websites use blue logos. Melancholy: Conversely, it can be associated with sadness, as in the idiom "feeling blue". Shades of Blue Light/Bright: Azure, Sky Blue, Cyan, Baby Blue, Cerulean. Dark/Subtle: Navy Blue, Indigo, Midnight Blue, Sea Foam. Blue in Fashion Blue is highly versatile, ranging from professional navy suits to casual denim jeans. Deep blues are often chosen for a "grown-up" or sophisticated, modern look. Types of Blue Pigments Prussian Blue: A deep, traditional blue pigment. Cobalt Blue: Known for its intense, vivid tone. Ultramarine: Historically made from lapis lazuli, a deep, rich blue. Common Idioms and Expressions Feeling blue: Feeling sad or depressed. Out of the blue: Something unexpected. Blue ribbon: Representing top quality or first place. True blue: Loyal and dependable. Other "Blue" References Music: "Blue" is a British boy band formed in 2000, known for hits like "All Rise". Computing: "Blue" is also a graphical computer music environment written in Java.

references.title: One of my most favorite colors in my Crayola crayons was periwinkle. Cobalt blue is a color I gravitate towards still after all these years. Cobalt, blue, and periwinkle each offer distinct hues within the blue spectrum, each bringing a unique quality to a color palette. Cobalt: This shade is a deep, intense blue with a striking brightness that almost leans toward electric. Cobalt has strong saturation, which makes it bold and eye-catching, often conveying energy and depth. Its vibrancy and richness stand out, making it ideal for adding visual weight to an artwork. Periwinkle: This color has a gentle, almost pastel quality. With a hint of lavender, it leans toward a cooler, softer end of the spectrum, giving it a calming and delicate appearance.
